author: reek
body: Builds an ACPI table set in a heap buffer and parses it. The bytes are laid down from the ACPI specification -- signatures, lengths, and every field at its spec offset -- not from the parser's own idea of where things live, so a parser that reads PM1a_CNT_BLK from the wrong offset reports the event block and fails here. The fixture's ground truth was generated independently in Python.

author: reek
body: SLP_TYPa is 5 and SLP_TYPb is 7, deliberately not the zero that QEMU's own _S5_ happens to carry: a driver that skips the AML decode and hardcodes the value it saw on one emulator cannot pass.

author: reek
body: Both root-table shapes are covered. A revision 0 RSDP offers only the RSDT and its 32-bit entries; a revision 2 RSDP offers the XSDT and its 64-bit entries and must be preferred. The final case corrupts one RSDP byte and expects the checksum to reject the whole thing.

author: reek
body: Every SDT header carries revision, an OEM id, an OEM table id, and an OEM revision. Their bytes matter only to the checksum, but the fixture writes real ones so it is a table a firmware could have published.

author: reek
body: MADT: local APIC address at 36, flags at 40, then a Type 0 processor entry (length 8) and a Type 1 I/O APIC entry (length 12) whose address sits four bytes into the structure.

author: reek
body: The RSDP is not an SDT: its signature is eight bytes, its first checksum covers only the first twenty, and revision 2 adds a length, a 64-bit XSDT pointer, and a second checksum over the whole thing.

author: reek
body: Table addresses are reported as offsets from the blob base, so the expected output does not depend on where the heap happened to be.

author: reek
body: Corrupting one byte of the OEM id leaves the signature intact and the revision intact, so only the checksum can catch it.

author: reek
body: A zero pointer is the honest "firmware exposed no ACPI" answer.

author: reek
body: The memory search, on a window of heap rather than on the BIOS area, so it runs anywhere. Four arms, and each fails for one reason only.

author: reek
body: The window is aligned up to 16 first: the scan steps by 16 from where it is told to start, and a window that began mid-paragraph would move every arm's answer for a reason that has nothing to do with the arm.

author: reek
body: Reported as an offset from the window, and 0 already means "not found", so a hit at offset 0 would be ambiguous. No arm places one there.
